pretext_or_consistency_target: NT-Xent on exercise-to-exercise and concept-to-concept graphs, at node level and graph level
positive_pair_definition: Two augmented views of the same graph (graph level), or the same node across those two views (node level)
negative_pair_definition: Other graphs at graph level, and other nodes at node level
augmentation: Random edge deletion or addition, node deletion, and attribute masking

pretext_or_consistency_target: Cross-entropy reconstruction of explicit question-skill edges, with a separate difficulty regression
positive_pair_definition: Not a contrastive pair. The target is the observed question-skill relation
negative_pair_definition: Not a contrastive pair. Non-edges enter the cross-entropy as the negative class of the relation
augmentation: No view augmentation. The pretext is reconstruction of the bipartite question-skill graph
evidence_locator: p.3, explicit question-skill loss L1; p.4, joint optimization

pretext_or_consistency_target: Contrastive loss on encoded question histories and interaction histories
positive_pair_definition: Two augmented views of the same learning history, s+1 and s+2
negative_pair_definition: Other histories in the batch, plus hard negatives made by changing responses
augmentation: Question mask, interaction crop, interaction permutation, and question replacement by an easier or harder question

pretext_or_consistency_target: Contrastive loss on knowledge states diagnosed from augmented learning histories
positive_pair_definition: Knowledge states from two augmented sequences of the same learner
negative_pair_definition: Knowledge states of other learners in the batch
augmentation: Flip response, drop item, and swap adjacent question-response pairs

pretext_or_consistency_target: InfoNCE between a node and its representation in an adaptively augmented hypergraph view
negative_pair_definition: Views of different nodes, with a further negative set of nodes that share a hyperedge
augmentation: Adaptive node dropout, with dropout probability adjusted by node importance

pretext_or_consistency_target: InfoNCE between the meta-path view and the neighbor-sampling view, and between the meta-path view and the KT view, of the same question
positive_pair_definition: The positive set P_i of the target question node in another view
negative_pair_definition: The remaining nodes N_i in that view
augmentation: Three relation views of one heterogeneous graph; non-question nodes are masked after meta-path sampling

pretext_or_consistency_target: InfoNCE between the meta-path channel and the network-schema channel of the same question node
positive_pair_definition: The two channel views of the same node
augmentation: No input augmentation. The two views are the meta-path channel and the network-schema channel
evidence_locator: p.5, InfoNCE on the two channels

pretext_or_consistency_target: InfoNCE, written with binary cross-entropy, between an observed student representation and a counterfactual student representation on the student-question-concept graph
positive_pair_definition: The student representation after the first counterfactual transformation
negative_pair_definition: A destructed transformation of the same student representation
augmentation: Counterfactual replacement of questions by similar questions, plus a destructive transformation used as the negative

pretext_or_consistency_target: InfoNCE between a state-hypergraph encoding and the encoding of its line graph, computed separately for global and local states
positive_pair_definition: A global or local state encoding and the corresponding line-graph encoding
negative_pair_definition: The same pair after row-wise and column-wise shuffling of the hypergraph
augmentation: No separate random view augmentation. Negatives are shuffled copies. Hyperedges are distilled from skill similarity and response patterns

pretext_or_consistency_target: Parent-child score on the knowledge hierarchy, together with cross-graph hierarchical contrast between the hierarchy and the association graph. The paper also names graph reconstruction as part of the same embedding stage
positive_pair_definition: A parent-child pair in the knowledge hierarchy
negative_pair_definition: Other nodes sampled as the negative set
augmentation: No stated node, edge, or sequence perturbation. The pairs come from the hierarchy and from the cross-graph alignment

pretext_or_consistency_target: InfoNCE between primary-encoder and momentum-encoder embeddings, plus a graph-structure constraint on connected question-concept pairs
positive_pair_definition: The same question node, or the same concept node, encoded by the primary encoder and by the momentum encoder
augmentation: No explicit augmentation. Views come from the intact bipartite graph through a momentum encoder
evidence_locator: Sec. 3.2 and Sec. 3.5; InfoNCE and graph-structure constraint

pretext_or_consistency_target: Mutual-information loss between a local node representation and the global summary of a temporal heterogeneous graph
positive_pair_definition: A node embedding and the global summary of the same graph
negative_pair_definition: A corrupted graph instance produced by an operator tau
augmentation: The negative graph is tau of the original features and adjacency. The paper does not name the corruption

pretext_or_consistency_target: Contrastive loss between coarse-view and fine-grained-view embeddings of the same question, plus a prototype contrastive loss
positive_pair_definition: The coarse-view embedding of a question and its fine-grained-view embedding; for the prototype term, the question and its cluster-center prototype
negative_pair_definition: Other question nodes, reweighted by clustering; prototype vectors outside the node's cluster
augmentation: Feature masking and edge masking on the fine-grained view
evidence_locator: Sec. 4.1, feature and edge masking; Sec. 4.4, Eqs. (15)-(16)

pretext_or_consistency_target: InfoNCE that the paper describes as encouraging consistency between a student's individual knowledge state and the common state of similar students
positive_pair_definition: The individual knowledge state of student u at step t and the common knowledge state of that student's similar students
negative_pair_definition: The other individual and common states in the mini-batch
evidence_locator: Sec. III-D, Eqs. (12)-(13). The paper names Lssf as InfoNCE

pretext_or_consistency_target: Contrastive loss on student answer sequences, with the denominator split into local-sample and overall-sample terms
positive_pair_definition: z+ , called the positive sample of answer-sequence sample f. The equation does not give z+ a further definition
negative_pair_definition: Local-sample terms and overall-sample terms in the denominator, with weight mu on the local term
augmentation: Skill replacement by difficulty order, and reordering inside a subsequence. A comparison table also reports masking and clipping
evidence_locator: Sec. 3.3, skill replacement; Sec. 3.4, Eq. (7); Sec. 4, reordering

pretext_or_consistency_target: InfoNCE-style loss between a node and the same node after bipartite-graph augmentation, summed over the exercise-concept graph and the two same-type correlation graphs
positive_pair_definition: The same node in the original graph and in the augmented graph of the same view
augmentation: Random edge addition and edge deletion with probability p
evidence_locator: Sec. 3.4, graph augmentation; Sec. 3.5, contrastive objective
